paras: The lynching of Joe Joiner took place at Hutto, Texas, near Taylor and Round Rock, in mid-October 1888, when a mob of masked men hanged Joiner, a Black man, to a tree. Joiner had been accused of attempting to assault a young white girl and had been captured and placed in the hands of the sheriff or officers. A Taylor dispatch carried the story to papers across the country, one of which headlined it "A Negro Brute Hanged by a Mob."

According to the Washington Evening Star, on Sunday evening Joiner attempted to assault the twelve-year-old daughter of S. W. Wolsey near Hutto and was stopped by the screams of the girl and her younger sister. A special telegram from Round Rock to the Austin Statesman gave the girl's age as ten and said she had been "criminally assaulted" before her sister came to her rescue.

Joiner fled on horseback, by the Statesman's account on a stolen horse, toward Round Rock. The Evening Star reported that a posse overtook him six miles from Hutto and shot him through the shoulder before capturing him. The Taylor wire said instead that he was arrested by the sheriff, and the Round Rock special that he was arrested near that town.

On the road to jail, the wire reported, a mob of masked men seized the prisoner and hanged him to a tree. The Round Rock special added that the masked men took him from the officers and carried him back to the scene of the alleged crime before hanging him. In the Evening Star's version the posse returned with him to Hutto, where he was hanged at 11 o'clock at night "by unknown parties."
No report of an inquest, of arrests of the lynchers, or of any official response appears in the coverage.

The Evening Star printed the first and fullest account on October 16 under the head "A Texas Lynching." A dispatch dated Taylor, October 16, ran the next days in the Wheeling Daily Intelligencer as "A Negro Lynched," in the Delaware Gazette as "A Negro Brute Hanged by a Mob," and in the Macon Beacon of Mississippi as "Joiner Didn't Reach the Jail." The same item appeared in news summaries in Maine and New Hampshire, and as late as October 25 and 26 in "The South" columns of Kansas papers, which dated the lynching only "recently."

Each version stated the accusation as fact, and the copies garbled the details: the wire printed the town as "Hulto," and one summary named the victim "Joseph Jomer" and placed the lynching at Taylor. The only Texas account found, the Austin Statesman's special under the head "Lynch Law," called Joiner "the rape fiend." A one-line brief carried in Rhode Island and North Carolina said Joiner was lynched "by citizens, indignant at his career of crime," though no report describes any earlier record.

The accounts differ on the girl's age, twelve in the Evening Star and the wire but ten in the Round Rock special, and on whether the assault was attempted or committed. They also differ on who held Joiner and where he died: a posse at Hutto in the Evening Star, the sheriff on the road to jail in the wire, and officers near Round Rock with the hanging at the scene of the crime in the Statesman. The wire's "yesterday" places the lynching on Monday, October 15, while the Evening Star's narrative runs straight from the Sunday-evening assault to an 11 p.m. hanging.

reader.title: Lynching of Joe Joiner
bases: A Black man in custody after an accusation was seized by a masked mob and hanged to a tree (A1, A5, A7).

Joiner was hanged by a 'mob of masked men' who took him from the sheriff or officers (A5, A7), or by 'unknown parties' after a posse brought him back (A1), in response to an accusation of assault on a white girl (A4).

Three independent reports, the Evening Star account (A1), the Taylor wire (A4, A7) and the Round Rock special to the Austin Statesman (A5), agree that Joiner was accused, captured and hanged by a mob.

accounts.label: Evening Star account
accounts.gist: Joiner attempted to assault the girl Sunday evening, fled on a horse, was overtaken by a posse 6 miles from Hutto and shot through the shoulder; the posse brought him back to Hutto, where 'unknown parties' hanged him to a tree at 11 p.m.

accounts.label: Taylor wire
accounts.gist: Joiner attempted an assault on a 12-year-old white girl, was arrested by the sheriff, and on the road to jail a mob of masked men seized and hanged him at 'Hulto' on Oct. 15.

accounts.label: Round Rock special (Austin Statesman)
accounts.gist: Woolsey's 10-year-old daughter was 'criminally assaulted'; Joyner stole a horse, was arrested near Round Rock, and a masked mob took him from the officers, carried him to the scene of the crime and hanged him.

No paper names the county; Hutto is placed near Taylor and Round Rock
